application.name: ofetch
application.summary: A type-safe, feature-rich wrapper around the Fetch API.
application.purpose: Provide a ergonomic, typed `$fetch`/`ofetch` client that automatically handles baseURLs, query parameters, request body serialization, response parsing, retries, timeouts, hooks and normalized errors.

applicationFacts: This is the unjs ofetch library: a small, typed wrapper around the global Fetch API.
The package exports a default ofetch instance, $fetch, typed fetch/raw/native/create entry points, plus types ($Fetch, FetchOptions, FetchResponse, FetchContext, FetchError, etc.).

createFetch(globalOptions) returns a $fetch function; $fetchRaw does the actual work, $fetch returns parsed _data only, $fetch.raw exposes response/_data, $fetch.native delegates to the underlying fetch, and $fetch.create builds derived instances with merged defaults.

Retry policy: GET/DELETE-like and other non-payload methods get one retry by default, payload methods get none; retryable statuses are 408/409/425/429/500/502/503/504 unless overridden via retryStatusCodes; retries are skipped for active aborts.

Response bodies are parsed based on responseType/detected content-type (json via destr, stream for text/event-stream, text for text/* and svg/xml/html/xhtml, otherwise blob), with optional custom parseResponse for JSON-like responses.

JSON-serializable request bodies are auto-stringified (URLSearchParams for x-www-form-urlencoded, JSON.stringify otherwise), and the default content-type/accept headers are set to application/json when not already provided.
FormData/URLSearchParams/stream bodies are passed through untouched; stream bodies automatically set duplex="half".
The library applies baseURL and query/params to string requests before sending; aborts are supported via AbortSignal and the timeout option via AbortSignal.timeout combined with the caller's signal.
Errors are normalized into FetchError with a formatted message ([METHOD] "URL": STATUS TEXT) and getter-based request/options/response/data/status/statusCode/statusText/statusMessage properties.
Hooks (onRequest, onRequestError, onResponse, onResponseError) are invoked in order and may be a single function or an array.

Tests spin up a local h3 server (ok/echo/post/binary/403/408/204/timeout routes) and spy on globalThis.fetch, covering success, errors, retries, timeouts, aborts, hooks, deep-merge defaults, headers and streaming bodies.
